01 / GEOMETRY & STEERING

Four mixtures, one direction

Purple line: manual world-coordinate steering. Target direction is a simulator setting, not an estimated DOA. Change steering alone to test localization errors.

18 cm between sides; 16 mm front/back spacing. Ideal omnidirectional plane-wave microphones with fractional delays. Head drawing is schematic: this array mode has no HRTF, head shadow or room reverberation.

02 / ALGORITHM COMPARISON

Choose the spatial filter

Real pretrained network, two independent 48 kHz streams. Model loads once. This monaural baseline may alter interaural cues; it is not a binaural neural model or a claim of current state-of-the-art performance.

Start runs a one-second noise-only calibration with the target muted.

What the beamformer receives

Only four microphone mixtures and an explicit noise-calibration flag. The filter does not receive the clean speech or noise stems. MVDR freezes its noise statistics after calibration; changing the noise field requires learning again.

Audio stays in this browser. The bundled passages are from one LibriSpeech speaker. This page isolates enhancement; audiogram fitting and hearing-loss illustration remain in the hearing-loss lab.

Equations & limitations · LaTeX supplement · Spatial evaluation

Where does localization fit?

A DOA estimator would supply steering updates. It needs a target-selection rule to avoid following a louder interferer. This version exposes manual steering and known target angles so we can isolate angular errors before adding localization and tracking. Future evaluation will report angular error and tracking lag separately from audio-path latency.
